initiatives.name: Administrative Expense Reduction Programme
initiatives.summary: British Land delivered a 9% (£7m) reduction in administrative expenses to £75m through rigorous cost base challenge, while continuing to leverage scale by onboarding new acquisitions and developments with minimal incremental cost.

evidence.title: Administrative Expense Reduction Programme

evidence.quote: We are pleased to have delivered a 9% (or £7m) reduction in administrative expenses this year to £75m as we have continued to rigorously challenge the cost base.

initiatives.name: 1 Appold Street (8 Exchange Square) Redevelopment
initiatives.summary: British Land committed, via its Broadgate joint venture, to the full redevelopment of 1 Appold Street, a 14-storey office-led scheme, concurrently with a 21-year pre-let to Herbert Smith Freehills Kramer for 268,000 sq ft (60% pre-let). A fixed-price design-and-build contract was signed with Skanska to provide cost certainty.

evidence.title: Design-and-Build Contract with Skanska for Cost Certainty

initiatives.name: Capital Recycling Strategy (Offices to Retail Parks)
initiatives.summary: British Land continues disciplined capital recycling, selling longer-let London offices and mature/non-core assets, reinvesting proceeds into earnings-accretive retail park acquisitions (£94m in FY26, including £73m retail parks) and best-in-class campus developments.

evidence.title: Capital Recycling from Mature Offices into Retail Parks
evidence.summary: British Land continues disciplined capital recycling, selling longer-let London offices and mature/non-core assets, reinvesting proceeds into earnings-accretive retail park acquisitions (£94m in FY26, including £73m retail parks) and best-in-class campus developments.
evidence.quote: This includes selling longer-let London offices, acquiring earnings accretive retail parks and investing in best-in-class campus developments on a de-risked, capital-light basis... Over the year, we acquired £94m of retail assets including £73m of retail parks, in addition to the £738m purchased in FY25.

initiatives.name: ERP Finance Transformation Programme (Oracle Fusion)
initiatives.summary: British Land is implementing a new Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system (Oracle Fusion) to transform core business systems, upgrading legacy systems, standardising tasks, streamlining processes, and including automation of key financial control processes. The programme is scheduled for implementation in 2027.

evidence.title: ERP Finance Transformation Programme (Oracle Fusion)

The programme is scheduled for implementation in 2027.
evidence.quote: The Committee has provided Board-level oversight of the new ERP programme to implement Oracle Fusion. The programme will transform the systems that facilitate our core business functions, by upgrading various legacy systems into a modern, high-performing ERP tool.

evidence.title: AI and Automation for Process Efficiency and Risk Management
evidence.summary: British Land is identifying opportunities to use AI and automation to streamline processes, enhance controls, and strengthen risk management, including leveraging a global risk tool within the new ERP system for automated control testing. An internal audit on 'Artificial Intelligence - Strategy and governance' was also completed during the year.
evidence.quote: Identify opportunities to use AI and automation to streamline processes, enhance controls and strengthen risk management within a responsible well-governed framework.

initiatives.name: Life Science REIT Acquisition
initiatives.summary: British Land made a recommended cash-and-share offer for Life Science REIT plc to enhance its Science and Technology presence across the Golden Triangle. The deal was expected to be immediately earnings accretive and non-dilutive to net tangible assets per share, completing in April 2026.

evidence.title: Recommended Acquisition of Life Science REIT plc

initiatives.name: UK Corporate Governance Code Provision 29 Compliance
initiatives.summary: British Land developed a roadmap and detailed risk and controls matrix to prepare for compliance with Provision 29 of the UK Corporate Governance Code, which requires Board attestation on risk and control framework effectiveness, applicable for the year ending 31 March 2027.

evidence.title: Preparation for UK Corporate Governance Code Provision 29
evidence.summary: British Land developed a roadmap and detailed risk and controls matrix to prepare for compliance with Provision 29 of the UK Corporate Governance Code, which requires Board attestation on risk and control framework effectiveness, applicable for the year ending 31 March 2027.
evidence.quote: Provision 29 is applicable for the Group's year ending 31 March 2027. It requires the Board to describe how it monitored and reviewed the risk and control framework, declare whether material controls were effective at the balance sheet date, and explain any material control weaknesses and remediation.

initiatives.name: Science-Based Net Zero Targets (SBTi)
initiatives.summary: British Land submitted new long-term science-based targets to SBTi for validation, aligned with a 1.5°C scenario, committing to 97% reduction in operational carbon intensity by 2040 and 90% reduction in absolute corporate emissions by 2050 against an FY24 baseline, replacing the current 2030 target.

evidence.title: New Science-Based Net Zero Targets Submitted to SBTi
evidence.summary: British Land submitted new long-term science-based targets to SBTi for validation, aligned with a 1.5°C scenario, committing to 97% reduction in operational carbon intensity by 2040 and 90% reduction in absolute corporate emissions by 2050 against an FY24 baseline, replacing the current 2030 target.
evidence.quote: We have submitted new, long term science-based targets to the Science Based Transition initiative (SBTi) for validation, aligned with a 1.5°C climate scenario. These commit us to reducing operational carbon intensity by 97% by 2040 and absolute corporate emissions (including embodied carbon and supply chain) by 90% by 2050, against our FY24 baseline.

initiatives.name: ESG Committee Dissolution and Governance Revision
initiatives.summary: British Land will dissolve its ESG Committee following the 2026 AGM, embedding ESG oversight into existing structures - the Audit Committee (renamed Audit & Risk Committee) takes on Health & Safety oversight, and the Remuneration Committee (renamed Remuneration & People Committee) takes on DE&I oversight, reflecting evolved strategy and embedded ESG considerations.

evidence.title: Dissolution of ESG Committee and Governance Framework Revision
evidence.summary: British Land will dissolve its ESG Committee following the 2026 AGM, embedding ESG oversight into existing structures - the Audit Committee (renamed Audit & Risk Committee) takes on Health & Safety oversight, and the Remuneration Committee (renamed Remuneration & People Committee) takes on DE&I oversight, reflecting evolved strategy and embedded ESG considerations.
evidence.quote: The Board agreed at the May 2026 Board meeting that from the conclusion of the 2026 AGM, a revised Governance Framework would take effect and the ESG Committee will be dissolved. ESG considerations are now embedded across the organisation as the Company's strategy has evolved and our commitment remains as strong as ever.

initiatives.name: Canada Water Masterplan Strategic Pivot
initiatives.summary: Following a Section 73 planning approval in March 2026, British Land intends to pivot future phases of the Canada Water Masterplan towards higher residential/living uses and a more capital-light model, including partnering with or selling plots to residential and student developers to accelerate returns.

evidence.title: Canada Water Masterplan Shift to Capital-Light, Living-Led Model
evidence.summary: Following a Section 73 planning approval in March 2026, British Land intends to pivot future phases of the Canada Water Masterplan towards higher residential/living uses and a more capital-light model, including partnering with or selling plots to residential and student developers to accelerate returns.
evidence.quote: Looking ahead, the next phases of the Masterplan are likely to have a higher living uses component and be more capital light for British Land. This will likely include partnering with or selling plots to residential and student developers to accelerate returns.
